components.name: Ribbon Tile
components.description: Labelled ribbon tool: a quiet icon (--ui-icon) over an 11px label, outlined on the paper. On is a 14% accent tint with an accent border; hover never uses the accent.
components.css: .ds-rb-btn { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; display: inline-grid; grid-template-rows: 18px auto; row-gap: 2px; align-content: center; justify-items: center; min-width: 44px; height: 44px; padding: 0 8px; border: 1px solid var(--border, #dcdcd6); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--bg, #ffffff); color: var(--text, #24292f); font-size: 11px; line-height: 1.15; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; } .ds-rb-btn svg { width: 18px; height: 18px; align-self: center; color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text, #24292f) 25%, var(--muted, #6e7781)); } .ds-rb-btn span { white-space: nowrap; } .ds-rb-btn:hover { background: var(--panel, #f4f4f2); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text, #24292f) 22%, var(--border, #dcdcd6)); } .ds-rb-btn:hover svg, .ds-rb-on svg { color: var(--text, #24292f); } .ds-rb-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #2f6feb); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-rb-btn:active { background: var(--panelAlt, #e8e8e4); } .ds-rb-on, .ds-rb-on:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent, #2f6feb) 14%, var(--bg, #ffffff)); border-color: var(--accent, #2f6feb); }

narrative.overview:
OpenTex is a calm, tidy desk. The paper is the brightest thing in the room: the editor sits on the pure background, the PDF page is a white sheet on a grey desk, and everything else (panels, ribbon, status bar) recedes into a slightly darker, warm-grey surface. Tools sit within reach and say what they are, but they don't compete with the writing. The playful parts, such as the pixel forest of Forest Timer or the plants of Writing Garden, are small things on the windowsill: they live inside their own panels and never leak into the chrome.

The chrome is native and restrained. It uses the operating system's own font at small sizes (13px body, 11px uppercase panel titles), flat surfaces separated by 1px lines, quiet hover tints, and a single accent color that marks the main action and the current selection. Density is that of a good desktop app, not a web page: 32px panel heads, 26px status bar, 3px-padded rows.

Every color is a theme variable. The same 14 interface keys and 6 syntax keys drive all 12 built-in themes (Light is the default) and any theme the user writes, so a design decision is only finished once it reads correctly in a dark theme and in High Contrast too.

It must not look like a web SaaS dashboard: no floating cards with soft shadows, no gradients, no big rounded pill buttons, no marketing hero layouts inside the app.
keyCharacteristics: The paper (editor background and PDF page) is the lightest, calmest surface; chrome sits one step darker.
System font, small sizes, uppercase letter-spaced labels for panel titles.
Flat surfaces divided by 1px lines; shadows only on things that float above the window.
One accent color per theme, used for the main action, selection and focus.
Everything is a theme variable; nothing is hard-coded to the Light theme.
Play is confined to plugin panels.

rules.name: The Paper Is Brightest Rule
rules.body: The writing surface (bg) and the PDF page are the lightest, calmest surfaces. Chrome uses panel, never bg, unless it is part of the paper (the active tab, the ribbon body, an input).

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each theme has one accent. Use it for the main action, selection, focus and "this is on"; never as decoration. Ribbon and toolbar icons are never accent (they use `--ui-icon`); the open ribbon tab is a 2px inset accent bar with a `--text` label. Tints of it come from `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) N%, transparent)` with N between 10% and 55%.

rules.name: The Theme Variable Rule
rules.body: UI code uses `var(--key)` and `var(--syn-key)` only. The only literal colors allowed are the white PDF page, black-alpha shadows and backdrops, and the fixed plugin-highlight hues in `styles.css`.

rules.name: The Small and Native Rule
rules.body: Chrome text stays between 11px and 14px in the system font. Anything larger belongs to the welcome page or to the paper.

rules.name: The Uppercase Is for Panels Rule
rules.body: Uppercase, letter-spaced 11px text means "this is the name of a panel or a section". Don't use it for buttons or content.

rules.name: The Only Floaters Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: If it is docked in the layout, it is flat. Shadows are for pages, menus, popovers, dialogs, bubbles and drag ghosts, in that vocabulary and nowhere else.

rules.name: The Inset for State Rule
rules.body: "Selected" and "flash" states use inset or outline rings in the accent (`inset 0 0 0 1px var(--accent)`, a 3px accent left bar), not drop shadows. "On" (a toggle, a chosen preset, an open popover's tile, Fit width in the PDF head) is the 14% accent tint plus a 1px accent ring; the ring carries the 3:1. Hover never uses the accent: it is panel or panelAlt and text-colored ink. Every control's keyboard focus is a 2px accent outline (`:focus-visible`).

rules.name: The Fit the Content Rule
rules.body: A ribbon button is no bigger than its icon and label need and no smaller than a comfortable target: no fixed widths, no empty two-line slots, no lone glyph in a big box.

dos: Do reference every color through `var(--key)` or `var(--syn-key)` and check new UI in Light, a dark theme and High Contrast.
Do keep the paper (bg) and the PDF page as the brightest, calmest surfaces; chrome uses panel.
Do separate docked areas with 1px border lines and tone, not shadows.
Do keep chrome text in the system font at 11–14px, with 11px uppercase letter-spaced (0.04em) labels for panel names.
Do reserve the filled accent button for the single main action in a view.
Do use the existing radii: 6px for controls and ribbon tiles, 8px for cards, 10px only for floating dialogs and popovers.
Do draw icons as 1.5px-stroke line SVGs in currentColor.
Do keep playful, illustrated or pixel-art content inside plugin panels.
donts: Don't make it look like a web SaaS dashboard: no floating cards with soft shadows, no gradients, no big rounded pill buttons, no hero layouts inside the app.
Don't add drop shadows to docked panels, tabs or ribbon tiles.
Don't hard-code Light theme hex values in UI code.
Don't use the accent as decoration or for more than one competing action per view.
Don't introduce web fonts for the chrome; the system font is the interface's voice.
